newsitem.title: USA: Average copper price seen near 105 cents/lb in '96.
newsitem.headline: Average copper price seen near 105 cents/lb in '96.

text.p: The average price of copper is expected to fluctuate two cents on either side of 105 cents in 1996 as the market heads for a world surplus of 90,000-100,000 short tons, said John Gross of the Copper Journal.
Gross also forecast an average price of 80-90 cents per pound for 1997 during a presentation to the American Copper Council meeting here.
Gross also expressed skepticism over industry forecasts calling for net new production to increase from 285,000 short tons in 1997 to 1.825 million short tons in the year 2000.
"I doubt very seriously that the majority of this is going to come onstream," he said.
